calls.head: The Wild should tilt the ice
calls.body: At 5-on-5, the Wild have been near the top of the league at getting more of the chances than they give up, and the Sharks one of the worst. The ice should tilt the Wild’s way, even if goaltending and bounces have the final say on the score.

MIN.head: We gave Minnesota a 77% chance, and they delivered.

SJS.head: We gave San Jose only a 23% chance, and it went the way we feared.

surprises.head: Minnesota couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: San Jose usually allows more dangerous shots than most teams. Not tonight: Minnesota’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 4.6% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.4% (about 6.8% against San Jose) and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 30 games.

story.head: Four points for Kaprizov as the Wild beat the Sharks
paras: Kirill Kaprizov opened the scoring for the Wild on the power play early in the first. Macklin Celebrini tied it up for San Jose midway through the second, but that was the last goal the Sharks would get. Maxim Shabanov put the Wild back ahead 2-1 on the power play just over two minutes later. Quinn Hughes made it 3-1 early in the third, and Zach Bogosian stretched the lead to 4-1 with just over six minutes left. Kaprizov finished with four points on a goal and three assists, and Hughes had a goal and two assists.

The Wild carried the play, outshooting the Sharks 29-24, and got the result to match. Jesper Wallstedt made 23 saves for the Wild, and Yaroslav Askarov stopped 25 of 29 at the other end. The Wild moved to 12-3-3, still first in the Central, while the Sharks dropped to 7-10-1, sixth in the Pacific.
